investigation.title: Remote Agent Creation Blocked by Swarm Agent Quota Limit (409 Conflict) — All Remote-Agents Checks Failing
investigation.summary: The AURA observability eval for remote-agent-create (and both sibling checks remote-agent-state and remote-agent-runtime) failed because POST /api/agents returned HTTP 409 with the error "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". The eval probe never received a created agent, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected and all contract assertions went unmet. This is an eval-infrastructure failure against the production-api endpoint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm backend rejected the eval's POST /api/agents request with a 409 Conflict because the org used by the observability probe has reached the swarm agent quota limit of 100. Because agent creation failed immediately (latencyMs=1354, well under the 30000ms warning threshold), the runner never obtained an agentId or vmId, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) unpopulated. All three remote-agents checks share the same upstream createAgent call and therefore all carry the identical 409 error message, consistent with a shared dependency failure at the quota-enforcement layer of POST /api/agents.

Lower probability — A transient swarm-side bug is misreporting the quota as exceeded when it is not; this would be disproved by inspecting the actual agent count for the probe org.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing with 409 Swarm Agent Quota Exceeded on POST /api/agents
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-state, remote-agent-create, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-17T07:27:09–11Z with an identical 409 conflict response from POST /api/agents indicating the swarm agent quota of 100 has been reached for the eval org. Because agent creation is the first step in the runner branch for all three checks, none of them can proceed past createAgent(), leaving all required evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) uncollected and the expected-output contract entirely unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm backend rejected POST /api/agents with HTTP 409 and error code "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". The eval runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1359) calls createAgent() as its first substantive action for every remote-agents check. Because that call fails immediately, no agent is created, no state is polled, and no evidence is written, causing all three sibling checks to fail with the same message. The root cause is a resource-quota exhaustion on the swarm backend for the eval org, not a code defect in the eval runner itself. This is an eval infrastructure failure; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigation.title: Image Generation Stream Eval Failure: SESSION_OPEN_FAILED (404) on production-api Runtime — Agent Harness Unreachable
investigation.summary: The image-generation-stream eval for the production-api runtime environment failed immediately with a SESSION_OPEN_FAILED error carrying a 404 status, indicating the agent runtime harness endpoint targeted by the eval runner is unreachable or misconfigured in that environment. The identical check passed in the desktop-release runtime at the same run time, proving the image generation pipeline itself is functional and isolating the failure to the production-api harness connectivity or configuration.
investigation.rootCause: The eval runner's call to /api/generate/image/stream in the production-api runtime environment received a 404 before any generation work could begin, causing a SESSION_OPEN_FAILED error frame. This is an eval infrastructure connectivity failure scoped to the production-api runtime: either the harness is not deployed, is deployed at a different URL than what SWARM_BASE_URL or LOCAL_HARNESS_URL resolves to in this environment, or the endpoint path /api/generate/image/stream does not exist at the targeted host for this runtime. No generation_completed frame or image URL was produced as a direct consequence. This is not evidence of a user-facing production outage; the desktop-release sibling check passed concurrently, confirming the underlying image generation capability is operational.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Creation Blocked by Swarm Agent Quota Limit (409 Conflict) — All Remote-Agents Checks Failing
investigations.summary: The AURA observability eval for remote-agent-create (and both sibling checks remote-agent-state and remote-agent-runtime) failed because POST /api/agents returned HTTP 409 with the error "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". The eval probe never received a created agent, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected and all contract assertions went unmet. This is an eval-infrastructure failure against the production-api endpoint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigations.rootCause: The swarm backend rejected the eval's POST /api/agents request with a 409 Conflict because the org used by the observability probe has reached the swarm agent quota limit of 100. Because agent creation failed immediately (latencyMs=1354, well under the 30000ms warning threshold), the runner never obtained an agentId or vmId, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) unpopulated. All three remote-agents checks share the same upstream createAgent call and therefore all carry the identical 409 error message, consistent with a shared dependency failure at the quota-enforcement layer of POST /api/agents.

failed-check.timing: latencyMs=1354, status=fail, endedAt=2026-06-17T07:27:09.761Z — request completed quickly, ruling out a timeout or VM boot hang

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:178-186: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready] — neither assertion could be evaluated because the agent was never created
possibleCauses: Primary — Swarm agent quota exhausted for the observability probe org: the 409 body explicitly states 'agent quota exceeded: limit is 100'. Previously created agents from prior eval runs (or other activity in the same org) were not cleaned up, filling the quota slot.

Secondary — Eval cleanup (withCleanup / track) failed to delete a previously created remote agent, leaving a leaked agent that counts against the quota. Repeated eval runs without successful cleanup would accumulate agents until the limit is hit.
Tertiary — The observability probe org was provisioned with a quota lower than expected, or the quota limit was recently lowered, causing the probe to hit the ceiling sooner than anticipated.
Lower probability — A transient swarm-side bug is misreporting the quota as exceeded when it is not; this would be disproved by inspecting the actual agent count for the probe org.

investigations.title: Image Generation Stream Eval Failure: SESSION_OPEN_FAILED (404) on production-api Runtime — Agent Harness Unreachable
investigations.summary: The image-generation-stream eval for the production-api runtime environment failed immediately with a SESSION_OPEN_FAILED error carrying a 404 status, indicating the agent runtime harness endpoint targeted by the eval runner is unreachable or misconfigured in that environment. The identical check passed in the desktop-release runtime at the same run time, proving the image generation pipeline itself is functional and isolating the failure to the production-api harness connectivity or configuration.
investigations.rootCause: The eval runner's call to /api/generate/image/stream in the production-api runtime environment received a 404 before any generation work could begin, causing a SESSION_OPEN_FAILED error frame. This is an eval infrastructure connectivity failure scoped to the production-api runtime: either the harness is not deployed, is deployed at a different URL than what SWARM_BASE_URL or LOCAL_HARNESS_URL resolves to in this environment, or the endpoint path /api/generate/image/stream does not exist at the targeted host for this runtime. No generation_completed frame or image URL was produced as a direct consequence. This is not evidence of a user-facing production outage; the desktop-release sibling check passed concurrently, confirming the underlying image generation capability is operational.
